Hertz.description: Hertz: SI frequency unit of one cycle per second.

Kilohertz.description: Kilohertz: frequency unit equal to one thousand hertz.

Megahertz.description: Megahertz: frequency unit equal to one million hertz.

Gigahertz.description: Gigahertz: frequency unit equal to one billion hertz.

Pascal.description: Pascal: SI pressure or stress unit equal to one newton per square meter.

Kilopascal.description: Kilopascal: pressure unit equal to one thousand pascals.

Megapascal.description: Megapascal: pressure or stress unit equal to one million pascals.

Bar.description: Bar: pressure unit equal to one hundred thousand pascals.

Atmosphere.description: Atmosphere: standard pressure unit equal to 101325 pascals.

Kelvin.description: Kelvin: SI unit of thermodynamic temperature on an absolute scale.

Celsius.description: Celsius: temperature scale with water freezing at zero degrees under standard conditions.

Joule.description: Joule: SI energy unit equal to one newton meter of work.

Watt.description: Watt: SI power unit equal to one joule per second.

Kilowatt.description: Kilowatt: power unit equal to one thousand watts.

Megawatt.description: Megawatt: power unit equal to one million watts.

Newton.description: Newton: SI force unit accelerating one kilogram by one meter per second squared.

Meter per second.description: Meter per second: SI speed unit measuring distance traveled per elapsed second.

Pascal-second.description: Pascal-second: SI dynamic viscosity unit relating shear stress to velocity gradient.

Mole.description: Mole: SI amount-of-substance unit counting a fixed Avogadro number of elementary entities.

Molarity.description: Molarity: solution concentration measured as moles of solute per liter.

Unit operation.description: Unit operation: physical processing step such as separation, mixing or heat exchange in a chemical plant.

Reaction kinetics.description: Reaction kinetics: dependence of chemical reaction rate on concentration, temperature and mechanism.

Mass transfer.description: Mass transfer: movement of chemical species driven by concentration or chemical-potential gradients.

Thermodynamics.description: Thermodynamics: relationships among energy, heat, work, entropy and equilibrium.

State of the art.description: State of the art: currently established methods and reported research baselines in a specified field.

PyTorch.description: PyTorch: tensor computing and automatic differentiation framework for training neural networks.
